newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Nov health spending up 0.1 pct vs Oct.
newsitem.headline: French Nov health spending up 0.1 pct vs Oct.

text.p: French healthcare spending in November rose 0.1 percent versus the previous month, the national health insurance fund, Caisse National d'Assurance Maladie (CNAM) said on Monday.
The CNAM said in a statement that the rise did not contradict the downtrend in spending established over the last six months.
The government has set a target of a rise of 2.1 percent in non-hospital spending in 1996.
In October, health spending fell 0.1 percent after a 0.4 percent drop in September, CNAM said.
The CNAM said when it released its September spending figures that health expenditures would have to fall for the rest of the year for it to meet its target.
Health spending in November was up 0.1 percent from December 1995 to November 1996, but down 0.5 percent on a November 1996 over November 1995 basis.
The French government is trying to curb health spending to cut its public deficits so it can meet Maastricht treaty targets for a single European currency.
CNAM said November non-hospital spending fell 0.4 percent compared with October, public hospital spending was up 0.5 percent and prescriptions fell 0.1 percent.
